### GitHub organization roles (tiered access)
| Role | Who | What it can do |
|---|---|---|
| **Owner** | Christopher today; Kevin, Anne, and David once they're comfortable (at minimum, Members) | Everything, including billing and adding people. Keep **at least 2–3 owners** so the org can never be orphaned. |
| **Member** | Trusted servants in active service roles | Sees private org repos as configured, joins teams (e.g. TechCom, LitCom, PR) |
| **Outside collaborator** | Volunteers helping on one project | Access to **specific repositories only**, without org membership. This is the tier TechCom uses for project helpers. |

## 🏛️ Committees & subcommittees

Committees, like individual meetings under the PIR umbrella, largely act autonomously.
Subcommittees sit under a parent committee. (In repos, folders are simply called `committees/`.)

| Committee | Subcommittees | Helpdesk |

| **Literature (LitCom)** | 12 Step Committee · Book Committee (ForaPIR) | `/litcom` → `litcom-desk` |
| **Public Relations (PR)** | 2026 Newsletter Committee (De Vine News) | `/pr` → `pr-desk` |
| **Tech (TechCom)** | — | `/techcom` → `techcom-desk`; GitHub matters → `/github` → `github-desk` |
| GSR · Convention · Finance · Intergroup · Service Structure Working Group | — | via `/techcom` or the committee's own channel for now |
| Board of Directors (501(c)(3)) | — | `board@` |
